# #124 — Entity graph lacks lifecycle tools (no delete/unlink) + get_entity UUID regex bug

State: CLOSED
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none
Created: 2026-06-18T04:40:17Z
Updated: 2026-06-18T04:58:09Z

## Summary

Follow-up to #122. The `ob_entities` graph is now writable and readable through public tools (`upsert_entity`, `link_entities`, `get_entity`, `list_entities`, `adjacent_context`), but it has **no lifecycle/removal surface** and one **validation bug**. Discovered while building the King Capital repo knowledge graph (16 entities, 41 links, all in `collab`).

These are all the same family of gap #122 addressed for *reads*: the entity store is a second-class citizen vs the legacy domain tables.

## 1. No way to delete/archive an entity

`archive_entry` (and `bulk_archive`) only accept the 5 legacy tables in their `table` enum:

```
"thoughts" | "decisions" | "relationships" | "projects" | "sessions"
```

Passing `{"table":"ob_entities","id":"..."}` is rejected at input validation:

```
MCP error -32602: Input validation error ... Invalid option: expected one of
"thoughts"|"decisions"|"relationships"|"projects"|"sessions"
```

There is **no public tool to remove an entity**, even with an admin token (the rejection is at schema validation, before any role check). A mistyped or test entity (e.g. an empty `king-core-TEST`) is stuck in the store permanently.

**Proposed:** add `archive_entity` / `delete_entity` (or extend `archive_entry`'s table enum to include `ob_entities`), with the same soft-delete `archived_at` semantics. `list_entities`/`search_brain` should exclude archived entities by default.

## 2. No way to remove a graph edge (unlink)

`link_entities` creates edges but there is no `unlink_entities` / `remove_link` / `delete_link`. Once a link is created it cannot be removed through the API. Re-running `link_entities` is idempotent (won't dup), but a wrong edge (wrong relation, wrong target) is permanent.

**Proposed:** add `unlink_entities` keyed the same way `link_entities` is idempotent (namespace + from_type + from_id + to_type + to_id + relation), or soft-delete by link id.

## 3. `get_entity` UUID regex rejects valid stored IDs

`get_entity`'s `id` schema requires the version nibble to be `[1-8]`:

```
/^([0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[1-8][0-9a-fA-F]{3}-[89abAB][0-9a-fA-F]{3}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}|...)$/
```

But the store contains entities whose UUID version nibble is `9+` (e.g. `649f5c00-c4d1-4f9b-a2eb-69536909f4b6` — the `9` after the 3rd group). `get_entity` 400s on these with `Invalid UUID`, **yet `list_entities`, `link_entities`, and `adjacent_context` accept the same IDs fine** and operate on them correctly. So the entity is real and reachable everywhere except `get_entity`.

**Proposed:** relax `get_entity`'s id pattern to match what the store actually mints / what the other entity tools accept (allow version nibble `1-9`, or just standard UUID with any version). Inconsistent validation across tools that take the same id type is the core problem.

## 4. (minor) `adjacent_context` does not hydrate neighbor names

Each link in the response carries `linked_id` + `linked_type` + `relation` + `direction`, but not the neighbor's `name`. Callers must join every `linked_id` back against `list_entities` to render a readable walk. Optionally include `linked_name` (and maybe `canonical_id`) in each link row.

## Repro

```bash
# 1. delete -> rejected
mcp2cli open-brain archive_entry --params '{"table":"ob_entities","id":"<id>"}'

# 2. unlink -> no such tool

# 3. get_entity regex bug
mcp2cli open-brain get_entity   --params '{"id":"649f5c00-c4d1-4f9b-a2eb-69536909f4b6"}'  # 400 Invalid UUID
mcp2cli open-brain list_entities --params '{"namespace":"collab"}'                          # returns that same id fine
mcp2cli open-brain adjacent_context --params '{"type":"entity","id":"649f5c00-c4d1-4f9b-a2eb-69536909f4b6","namespace":"collab"}'  # works
```

## Priority

Low-to-medium. The graph is fully usable for build-up today (writes, links, reads, traversal all work). These gaps bite on **cleanup and correction** — you can build the graph but you can't tidy it. #1 and #3 are the most useful to fix.
